answer: A claimant posts a 47-coin bond and collects a clerk-fired opal bead whose internal fracture map is published as 11 landmarks. At first light they climb the east fire ridge, press the bead into a painted spiral datum on the bedrock, and radio a live 6-minute clerk video call that must keep the bead and datum in frame. Peers recompute the fracture hash and overlay the call stills on a published 3-D scan, matching all 11 landmarks within 0.8 mm. A swapped bead or a call placed off the datum slashes the bond, so each alias needs its own climb and its own fired stone.
